title: Establish that the yoloxx20 baseline is not held out on val_half
description:
val_half is the second temporal half of the MOT20 *train* sequences. Determine
whether the published baseline detector trained on those frames.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 0, `datasets/README.md`.
close_reason:
Done, and the answer is yes. This is a material correction to every
cross-detector number in the project.

`bytetrack_x_mot20.tar` is ByteTrack's MOT20 *test* model, trained on
`mix_mot20_ch` = the full MOT20 train set plus CrowdHuman. val_half is the
second half of that train set, so the baseline has seen every frame it is
scored on. The RF-DETR arms have not.

Verified three ways. (1) val_half images are byte-identical to the original
train frames: md5 of frame 1 and the last frame of each sequence matches
MOT20-01[216,429], -02[1393,2782], -03[1204,2405], -05[1659,3315]. (2) The
`yoloxx20` variant manifest reads exactly
`datasets/val_half/{sequence}/det_yoloxx20/det_yoloxx20.txt` for 580,369
detections, which equals those four files' row count. (3) `datasets/README.md`
already labelled them "YOLOX-X detections from the MOT20-trained detector" and
warned they "should not be treated as clean detector holdout measurements".

Corroborating: BoostTrack's own `default_settings.py` selects
`bytetrack_x_mot20.tar` only when `args.test_dataset` is set, otherwise falling
back with the comment "Just use the mot17 test model as the ablation model for
20". And ByteTrack publishes no MOT20 half-split ablation model at all.

Consequence: every RF-DETR-vs-YOLOX delta is a LOWER BOUND. Arm D's +0.569 HOTA
is a win over a detector that had the answers. Arm-to-arm deltas are unaffected.

Root cause of the documentation failure: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` recorded
Stage 1 as "held out for both detector and ReID", true of the RF-DETR side
only, and every downstream document inherited it. Corrected in three files.

title: Decision: whether to produce MOT20 test tracks now
description:
Phase 9 was recorded as blocked on a scope call, framed when the best RF-DETR
configuration reached HOTA 68.81 against the baseline's 70.21 and the residual
gap needed a retrain.

THE PREMISE OF THAT BLOCK NO LONGER HOLDS. Arm D leads at 70.777, and per
e5-leakage that margin is a lower bound. The I4 competition build is training
now. The question is therefore live again rather than blocked, and it is a
human call.

Sub-decisions: which checkpoint (arm D, or the I4 competition final), and which
ReID (fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20 is BoostTrack++ as published and stronger; generic
OSNet keeps the detector comparison controlled across both stages).

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md`, `docs/results-reference.md` section 7.

title: Decision: initialize the competition build from base weights, not arm D
description:
Arm D is the best checkpoint so far. Decide whether the competition build
warm-starts from it or retrains from the shared base checkpoint.
close_reason:
Decided 2026-09-08 by the user: fresh from base with arm D's recipe.

Rationale. Arm D's `checkpoint_best_total.pth` was selected using val_half as
validation, and val_half is now inside the competition build's training set.
Warm-starting would inherit a checkpoint selection made on data the run then
trains on. Retraining from `rf-detr-xxlarge.pth` keeps provenance clean and
matches the 2026-09-06 two-build decision, in which the ablation chooses the
recipe and the epoch count while the competition build re-trains on the fuller
data.

Cost of the choice: about 2.5-3 hours rather than the 2-3 a warm start would
have taken.

title: Decision: exclude MOT17 and the yoloxx17 baseline from scope
description:
`bytetrack_x_mot20.tar` trained on val_half, so it is not a held-out baseline.
`det_yoloxx17` detections are already on disk and are what BoostTrack itself
uses for MOT20 validation. Decide whether to adopt them.
close_reason:
Decided 2026-09-08 by the user: do not use yoloxx17 at all; this project is not
concentrating on MOT17.

Accepted consequence, stated deliberately rather than discovered later: no
clean external baseline is available, so the yoloxx20 leakage caveat is
PERMANENT rather than pending. Every cross-detector delta in this repository
carries it indefinitely, and the trustworthy comparisons are RF-DETR
arm-to-arm, which share byte-identical manifests.

The only in-scope way to remove the caveat would be training YOLOX-X on
mot20_train_half ourselves; tracked as d-clean-baseline.

title: Audit the Byte65 MOT20-test supervision before using it
description:
21 MOT20-test-derived images were proposed for the training mix. Test-derived
supervision permanently changes what may be claimed about any resulting model,
so it needs a human audit and an explicit classification before use.

Evidence: `finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-byte65nms-68seq-audit.md`,
`docs/MOTPolicy.md`.
close_reason:
Done. 21 images human-audited with `byte65_human_audit_authority =
user_confirmed` recorded in every dataset audit that uses them.

Consequence, and the reason this issue mattered: every build containing these
images carries `classification = local_test_adapted` and
`held_out_benchmark_comparable = false`. No result from any arm in this
repository is leaderboard-comparable, independent of the separate yoloxx20
leakage problem. `docs/MOTPolicy.md` holds the required language.

title: Export arm C's detections and measure its duplicate rate
description:
The phenomenon is established; the cause is not.

Established: arm A emits 33.219 overlapping pairs per frame at IoU >= 0.75 in
4,463 of 4,463 frames. The control now exists — `tracking/scripts/analyze_gt_overlap.py`
applies the identical pairwise rule to `gt.txt`, where every box is a distinct
annotated person, and finds 0.585 pairs per frame (42.06% of frames, max GT-GT
IoU 0.983). So real crowding accounts for under 2% of the observed rate and
~32.6 pairs per frame are unexplained. NMS at IoU 0.70 removes them, worth
+0.63 HOTA.

Not established: whether MOT20's density (137.8 instances/image, ~19x COCO) or
CrowdHuman's sparsity (81% of training images averaging 22.7 persons) drives it.
Arm A and arm D are both CrowdHuman-heavy and cannot separate the two.

Do:
1. Export arm C's detections at `-t005`. Arm C trained on MOT20 only, no
   CrowdHuman, so its duplicate rate is the discriminating measurement. Same
   rate implicates density; a sharp drop implicates the training mix and makes
   this a data question rather than an architectural one.
2. Extend `analyze_detections.py` to match predictions to GT and count
   predictions-per-GT directly, across score thresholds. The GT control bounds
   the confound; matching removes it. The current figure counts raw prediction
   pairs and does not distinguish two boxes on one person from two boxes on two
   overlapping people.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 2.3,
`artifacts/tracking/gt-overlap-val_half.json`, `docs/results-reference.md`
sections 1.2b and 4.

title: I4 competition build training run, seven GPUs
description:
ByteTrack parity: train on the build that folds val_half into the training mix,
from base weights using arm D's recipe, taking the final checkpoint.

One GPU is held free for concurrent inference work.

Evidence: `finetuning/experiments.md`,
`finetuning/configs/rfdetr_2xl_i4-competition-maxsize1600-7gpu.toml`.
design:
Initialization is the base checkpoint, not arm D's weights. Arm D is the
ablation that selected this recipe and its epoch count; using its checkpoint
would inherit a selection made on val_half, which is now training data.

Seven GPUs (devices 0-6), device 7 held free. Effective batch is 4 x 2 x 7 =
56 rather than 64, because 7 does not divide 64. Step counts here are therefore
not interchangeable with arm A-D step counts at face value.

Eight epochs at 505.75 steps/epoch is about 4,046 optimisation steps, matched
against arm D's 3,730-step peak and landing inside arm D's plateau. Matching on
steps rather than epochs is the convention across this workstream because
images per epoch differ up to 8x between arms.
notes:
DELIVERABLE DECLARED IN ADVANCE, 2026-09-08, mid-run, after external review
flagged that "final checkpoint" was underspecified for a run with no validation
metric.

The deliverable is `last_ema.pth` — the final EMA weights.

Why this needs saying before the run ends: with a formally empty `valid` split
there is no metric to select on, but RF-DETR's `best_model.py` still writes
plausible-looking files. `checkpoint_best_ema.pth` is documented to be
"backfilled with the final EMA weights if the EMA metric never improved", which
is exactly this case. A file named `best` from this run is a backfill, not a
selection, and reporting it as "best" would be false.

EMA rather than the regular branch because arm D's ablation selected EMA
(`best_total_source = ema`, peak 0.6282 EMA vs 0.6243 regular) and this build
exists to enact arm D's recipe.

On completion:
  - record sha256 of `last_ema.pth` in `finetuning/experiments.md`
  - assert `checkpoint_best_*.pth` are NOT reported as selected
  - the run's config sha256 is `7d9d58cd...`, pinned in run-provenance.json;
    the config file must stay byte-identical until the run ends

Also corrected in `finetuning/experiments.md`: the config header's step
arithmetic said 505.75 steps/epoch and ~4,046 total. The true figures are 506
and 4,048, because `GradAccumAlignedDataset` pads 28,322 images up to 28,336 (a
multiple of 56) rather than truncating. The config file itself is deliberately
left unedited to preserve the provenance hash.
close_reason:
Done. Completed 2026-09-08 12:28:47, train_call_wall_seconds 8,983.98 (2h30m),
clean exit ("Trainer.fit stopped: max_epochs=8 reached") with launcher-result.json
written, which is this workstream's only trustworthy completion marker.

Delivered checkpoint: last_ema.pth
  sha256 fb3f2f0dba7d3b236652d0ae02c1d19874ee4c5f26145d853fe4ac63ec25ceb6
  epoch 8, global_step 4048

Ran on GPUs 0-6 with device 7 held free as instructed; the reserved card carried
concurrent arm-C detection export and never contended with training.

Three things worth recording:

1. The pre-declared checkpoint trap occurred exactly as predicted. The console
   log's final line is "EMA metric never improved; saved final EMA weights as
   checkpoint_best_ema.pth". With a formally empty valid split there was no
   metric to select on, so no checkpoint_best_total.pth or
   checkpoint_best_regular.pth was written at all, and checkpoint_best_ema.pth
   is a backfill rather than a selection.

   Verified rather than assumed: last_ema.pth and checkpoint_best_ema.pth hold
   IDENTICAL weights - 532 tensors compared, zero differing, both reporting
   global_step 4048. So the exposure was mislabelled provenance, not wrong
   weights. Declaring the deliverable in advance changed the record, not the
   model. checkpoint_best_ema.pth must still never be reported as "best".

2. The step arithmetic is settled empirically. The checkpoint's own global_step
   is 4048, matching 506 steps/epoch x 8 and refuting the config header's
   "about 4,046 at 505.75 steps per epoch". GradAccumAlignedDataset pads 28,322
   images up to 28,336 (a multiple of the 56 effective batch) rather than
   truncating. External review caught this; the run confirmed it.

3. The config file was deliberately never edited during the run. Its sha256
   7d9d58cd... is pinned as config_sha256 in run-provenance.json and still
   matches, so the provenance link is intact. The corrected arithmetic went
   into the receipt instead.

This model has NO held-out yardstick by construction: val_half is in its
training mix, so no figure in docs/results-reference.md can be re-measured
against it. That does not affect arms A-D, whose weights are untouched.

Evidence: finetuning/experiments.md "Completed: I4 Competition Build".

title: Phase 8b: root-cause the HOTA deficit
description:
Determine whether the deficit came from tracker integration, ReID, association
settings, annotation conventions, or the detector itself, before spending any
GPU time on a retrain.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Root-cause analysis",
`docs/results-reference.md` sections 1.2, 4, 5, 6.
close_reason:
Done, and it changed the framing of the whole project.

Ruled out: annotation conventions (val_half COCO labels are byte-identical to
gt.txt at mean IoU 0.9995); tracker-side degradation (mean matched IoU is
0.8334 before the tracker and 0.8343 after, so no post-detection stage harms
box quality); and detector superiority itself (under one pycocotools protocol
the baseline has the higher mAP@50:95, 0.6759 against 0.6297).

Established: the deficit is detector box regression. Edge residuals are
symmetric jitter at 1.22-1.46x the baseline's, with signed means near zero, so
there is no correctable offset. The earlier framing of "better detection, worse
tracking" was wrong; RF-DETR led only at IoU 0.5.

Also produced the per-stage instrumentation showing RF-DETR hands the tracker
283.5 raw boxes per frame against the baseline's 130.0, and 52.3 unmatched
tracks per frame against 27.1.

title: Decision: maintain two dataset builds, ablation and competition
description:
I4 removes the only held-out evaluation this repository has. Decide how to get
ByteTrack parity without losing the ability to compare Tier 1 experiments.
close_reason:
Decided 2026-09-06 by the user. Maintain two builds and two checkpoints, which
is what ByteTrack itself does: half-split ablations, full-train final model.

Ablation build = mot20_train_half + CrowdHuman + Byte65, evaluated on val_half
which stays held out, used to compare I5/I6/I7. Competition build =
ablation plus mot20_val_half, no local evaluation, for MOT20 test tracks only.

The competition build trains for an epoch count chosen on the ablation build and
takes the FINAL checkpoint; its valid split is a formality for the training loop
and must not drive checkpoint selection. Given the epoch-5 peak already observed,
that epoch count is a real experimental output of the ablation build, not a
default.

Both builds carry `classification = local_test_adapted` regardless, because of
the 21 Byte65 MOT20-test images.

title: Fix embedding cache keying so variant swaps cannot reuse stale vectors
description:
Upstream keys its embedding cache by sequence name alone
(`./cache/embeddings/{video}_embedding.pkl`, loaded via `tag.split(":")[0]`).
Its only guard compares cached embedding count against detection count.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Cache-keying hazard".
close_reason:
Done. The upstream guard cannot detect a changed ReID model over unchanged
detections: the counts match and stale vectors from the previous model are
returned silently, which would have corrupted every comparison in this project
without ever raising an error.

Caches are now keyed by detection variant and ReID variant together. This was
treated as a precondition for any grid work rather than an optimisation. The
ECC cache is exempt because its contents depend only on the images.

title: Share one long-side cap between training and detection export
description:
A checkpoint trained at a raised `max_size` and exported at the library default
would silently produce detections from geometry the model never saw. Export and
training must read the same value.

Evidence: `finetuning/src/mot20/detection/rfdetr_training.py`,
`finetuning/tests/detection/test_rfdetr_training.py`.
close_reason:
Done. `apply_long_side_cap(max_size)` mutates `rfdetr.datasets.coco._COCO_MAX_SIZE`
and returns the cap in force; both `finetuning/scripts/train_rfdetr_2xl.py` and
`tracking/scripts/export_detections.py` call it, and the export records the
result in its manifest's `geometry.max_size`.

It rejects non-integers, booleans, non-positive values, and anything not
divisible by the 40 px window stride. Ordering matters and is commented in the
export: the cap is a module-global read when the validation transform is built,
so it must be applied before dataset construction.

Verified live during arm D: both the training console and the export log print
"long-side cap in force: 1600px", and the export's mAP checksum reproduced
0.6280 against the recorded 0.6282. Covered by `LongSideCapTest`.

title: I8: compare CrowdHuman's box convention against MOT20's
description:
Phase 8b proved the *validation* labels are byte-identical to gt.txt at mean
IoU 0.9995. It never checked the *training* labels, and CrowdHuman is 81% of
them. CrowdHuman full-body boxes are amodal annotator estimates of occluded
extent, produced by a different process than MOT20's.

If the conventions differ systematically, that is a second mechanism for the
localization jitter and it changes what a mix experiment should look like.

Compare on a normalised basis: aspect ratio, visible-to-full ratio, and how
each treats truncation at the image border. No GPU required, and it targets the
largest remaining gap (LocA 2.856).

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I8,
`docs/experiment-report.md` section 3.

title: Arm D: raise the training long-side cap to 1600
description:
I6 arm. Same dataset as arm A with byte-identical manifests, changing only the
effective input geometry, so any difference is attributable to resolution.

Evidence: `finetuning/experiments.md`, `docs/results-reference.md` section 3.4,
`docs/experiment-report.md`.
close_reason:
Done, `rfdetr-2xl-i5-armd-2026-09-07-r1`, 27,256.6 s, 30 epochs, micro-batch 4
x grad_accum 2 x 8 GPUs, 14 GB of 24 GB per card, no OOM.

Peak EMA mAP@50:95 0.6282 at epoch 9; peak regular 0.6243 at epoch 13;
`checkpoint_best_total.pth` has `best_total_source = ema` at global_step 3730.
The only arm to beat arm A.

Carried through the full chain to HOTA on val_half with held-out OSNet ReID and
BoostTrack++ defaults: HOTA 70.777 against the baseline's 70.208 and arm A's
68.809. The first configuration in the project to beat the baseline.

The mechanism contradicts the stated rationale, which is the important part.
I6 was proposed to fix box regression; LocA moved 85.190 -> 85.321, by 0.131,
and is still 2.856 below the baseline. The gain is association, AssA +2.810
over arm A, reached through recall: DetRe 76.952 -> 78.256, 8,082 fewer false
negatives, IDSW 1,571 -> 1,262, Frag 4,289 -> 3,704, IDF1 83.255 -> 85.637.

Resolution also failed to fix duplicate predictions: 31.4 duplicate pairs per
frame against arm A's 33.2, still in 100% of frames.

title: Gate detection export on reproducing the recorded training mAP
description:
`RFDETR.predict()` resizes to a square, whereas training used aspect-preserving
resize with a long-side cap. Exporting through the wrong path would silently
degrade every downstream number with no error.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Detector geometry gate",
`artifacts/tracking/geometry-gate-rfdetr2xl-e5.json`.
close_reason:
Done. Before any bulk export, the epoch-5 checkpoint was re-evaluated through
RF-DETR's own `evaluate()` path: mAP@50:95 0.6209 against the 0.6202 recorded
during training, and `val/loss` 6.0158 against 6.0166.

The export then captures detections from that same verified loop, so the
reported mAP is a checksum on the export rather than a separate claim. Repeated
for arm D, which reproduced 0.6280 against a recorded 0.6282 while printing
"long-side cap in force: 1600px".

title: Generate the results reference from artifacts and write the report
description:
Reported numbers must not be transcribed by hand, and the interpretation needs
somewhere to live that is separate from the numbers.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/build_results_reference.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md`, `docs/experiment-report.md`.
close_reason:
Done. `tracking/scripts/build_results_reference.py` reads every figure from a
manifest, metrics CSV, or annotation file and emits `docs/results-reference.md`,
so the document cannot drift from the artifacts and cannot contain a remembered
number. It is regenerated after every new experiment and must never be hand-edited.

`docs/experiment-report.md` is the interpretation layer: the detection matrix
and the TrackEval tracking matrix side by side against the baseline, with
conclusions, citing the generated file for every value.

One generator subtlety worth keeping: association-sweep runs carry explicit
`applied_overrides`, but the earlier det_thresh runs baked the setting into the
tracker slug, so reading only the overrides rendered three different runs as
"defaults". `settings_label()` handles both. And `launcher-result.json` is the
only trustworthy completion marker, because a run that died at its last
scheduled epoch would otherwise look finished.

title: Agent harness, repository policy, and work tracking
description:
Cross-agent operating rules, the repository-specific factual overlay under
`.claude/project/`, and the durable work tracker.

Evidence: `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/project/`, `.beads/beads.md`.

title: I7a: fix the training schedule that makes every arm decay
description:
All four arms peak in single-digit epochs and then decline monotonically for
the remainder of the run. Arm A lost 0.037 mAP over its last 45 epochs. This is
compute being spent to make the model worse, reproduced on every mix and at two
different input resolutions, and no hypothesis has been tested.

`lr_scheduler = "step"` with `lr_drop` at 24 or 40 never fires usefully because
the peak arrives long before the drop. A short cosine run is the obvious
candidate and is the cheapest training experiment available, because it is
short by construction.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` sections 3.1-3.4,
`docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I7.

title: I6: test whether raising the training long-side cap closes the gap
description:
Arm D against arm A with byte-identical manifests, changing only geometry.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I6,
`docs/experiment-report.md`.
close_reason:
Done. I6 WORKS, BUT NOT BY ITS STATED MECHANISM.

Arm D reaches HOTA 70.777 against the baseline's 70.208 and arm A's 68.809 —
the first configuration in this project to beat the baseline, +0.569 and +1.968
respectively. Also ahead on MOTA (+2.945), IDF1 (+3.101), Frag (-1,539) and MT
(+150).

The mechanism contradicts the rationale. I6 was proposed to fix box regression.
LocA moved 85.190 -> 85.321, by 0.131, and remains 2.856 below the baseline,
even though mAP@75 on the exported checkpoint improved 0.7400 -> 0.7523. That
mAP gain did not survive contact with the tracker's operating point.

The gain is association: AssA +2.810 over arm A, now exceeding the baseline's
by 1.642. The route is recall, DetRe 76.952 -> 78.256 and 8,082 fewer false
negatives, giving the tracker more continuous evidence per identity.

So the localization deficit is real, unfixed, and still the largest single gap
to the baseline. It is simply no longer the binding constraint on HOTA.
Precision remains the other weakness: DetPr 82.300 against 87.688, 21,242 false
positives against 6,947.

title: I5: test whether the CrowdHuman/MOT20 mix causes the early peak
description:
Three single-variable arms sweeping the MOT20 share across essentially its
whole range, on the ablation build so val_half stays a valid yardstick.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I5,
`docs/results-reference.md` sections 3.1-3.3.
close_reason:
Done. HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED.

MOT20 share 18.8% -> 48.0% -> 100% gives peak mAP@50:95 0.6202 / 0.6168 /
0.6139. That is a spread of 0.0063, about 1% relative, and it moves the WRONG
way: the unmodified arm A is the best of the three. All three arms reproduce
the same early-peak-then-monotone-decline shape, so removing CrowdHuman
entirely does not fix it.

Two consequences. The measured reasoning about scale and density regimes, while
correct as measurement, does not predict the outcome, and is retained as a
recorded hypothesis that testing rejected. And the post-peak decline is not the
training mix, which raised the prior on I6 and led directly to arm D.

One claim from this issue was later corrected: the duplicate-prediction rate
cannot be attributed to arm C, because arm C's detections were never exported.
See e5-armc-duplicates.

title: Audit the RF-DETR data transform, target retention, and collator padding
description:
Establish what geometry the model actually sees, because the configured
`resolution` is not necessarily what binds.

Evidence:
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-rfdetr-loader-geometry-audit.md`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 4.3.
close_reason:
Done, and it produced the single most consequential finding in the detector
workstream. The training transform is `RandomResize([1120],
max_size=_COCO_MAX_SIZE)` with `_COCO_MAX_SIZE = 1333`. At MOT20's 1920x1080
the 1333 cap binds, not the 1120 target: the model sees 1333x750, a scale of
0.694, and the `resolution = 1120` setting is inert.

The baseline YOLOX-X runs `test_size = (896, 1600)` -> 1593x896, scale 0.830,
and therefore sees every pedestrian about 20% larger. That gap became I6, and
arm D closed it by setting `max_size = 1600` for an effective 0.833.

title: Build a standalone BoostTrack++ runner over the artifact store
description:
Upstream `main.py` couples detection, embedding, tracking, and output. A runner
that consumes stored L1 and L2 artifacts is required for a composable grid, and
must not change tracker behaviour.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/run_boosttrack.py`,
`docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Local changes to repos/BoostTrack".
close_reason:
Done. `tracking/scripts/run_boosttrack.py` drives BoostTrack++ from stored
detections and embeddings, with the tracker itself unmodified in behaviour.
Includes the detection scale fix and the non-strict OSNet load asserting the
missing keys are exactly `{classifier.weight, classifier.bias}`.

Per-stage instrumentation in `tracking/scripts/diagnose_stages.py` hooks record
and delegate, so tracker behaviour is unchanged while producing the per-frame
stage counts in `docs/results-reference.md` section 6.

Note `repos/` is git-ignored, so local tracker changes are documented in
`docs/tracker-experiments.md` rather than committed.

title: Arm A: 50-epoch baseline fine-tune at the 1333 cap
description:
The first full fine-tune and the reference every later arm is compared against.

Evidence:
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-rfdetr-2xl-byte65-aspect-full-50e.md`,
`finetuning/experiments.md`, `docs/results-reference.md` section 3.1.
close_reason:
Done, `rfdetr-2xl-byte65-test-adapted-ddp-batch8-lr5e5-aspect-full-50e-2026-09-04-r1`,
42,703.70 s, 50 epochs, 8 GPUs.

Peak regular mAP@50:95 0.6202 at epoch 5 of 50; peak EMA 0.6198 at epoch 8;
final epoch 49 regular 0.5832. `checkpoint_best_total.pth` came from the
regular branch at global_step 2238.

The result that shaped everything after it: accuracy peaked at epoch 5 and then
declined monotonically for 45 more epochs, losing 0.037 mAP, with `val/loss`
back at its epoch-0 level by epoch 49. Carried through to HOTA 68.809 with
held-out OSNet ReID.

No `console.log` survives: the launcher teed from the host into a
container-created root-owned directory, which failed silently. Fixed for arms
B/C/D by teeing inside the container.

title: Score every detection variant under one pycocotools protocol
description:
Neither detector's own evaluation code can be trusted for a cross-detector
comparison. Score both through identical pycocotools against the same
annotations.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/analyze_detections.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 4.1.
close_reason:
Done for six variants including arm D, completed 2026-09-08. Same `valid`
annotations, MOT20 ignore regions carried as `iscrowd`, `maxDets = 390` for
every variant.

Required reading the COCOeval accumulator directly: pycocotools' `summarize()`
computes the headline AP with a hardcoded `maxDets = 100` that is absent from
this list and silently yields -1.

Result: the baseline wins mAP@50:95 for both arms — 0.6759 against arm A's
0.6297 and arm D's 0.6351 — while RF-DETR wins mAP@50, up to 0.9663 against
0.9000. A crossover at IoU threshold, which is the signature of a localization
deficit rather than a recall deficit. Arm D improves every mAP column over arm
A, with the largest gain at mAP@75 (+0.0120), and still does not change the
verdict.

title: Build the layered L0-L4 artifact store with manifests
description:
A tracking result is a composition of detector, ReID model, and tracker
settings. Storing only end results makes the grid unreproducible and forces
recomputation whenever one factor changes.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Artifact Levels and Variant Naming".
close_reason:
Done, under `artifacts/tracking/`: L0 ECC, L1 detections per detector variant,
L2 embeddings per detector+ReID pair, L3 tracks per full combination, L4
metrics. Every level writes a manifest, so any cell of the grid is reproducible
from its path plus its manifests.

Two design decisions that carried weight. L2 embeddings are computed for every
exported detection rather than only those surviving a tracker's `det_thresh`,
which makes them independent of tracker configuration and is what makes the
grid composable at all. And the published YOLOX detections already present
under `datasets/val_half/<sequence>/det_yoloxx20/` are registered as an
ordinary detector variant rather than a special case, so the baseline is one
cell of the same grid and runs through identical code.

title: I1: sweep suppression IoU and adopt greedy NMS at 0.70
description:
RF-DETR exports without NMS by design. Test whether that is right for MOT20.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I1,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 7.1.
close_reason:
Done. Suppression IoU none / 0.70 / 0.60 / 0.50 gives HOTA 68.175 / 68.809 /
68.510 / 66.076. Adopted 0.70, which matches the `nmsthre` the published YOLOX
detections were produced with, worth +0.63 HOTA.

The finding that mattered beyond the setting itself: NMS *lowers* mAP@50:95
(0.6337 -> 0.6297) while *raising* HOTA. COCO AP tolerates extra low-ranked
duplicates that a tracker must resolve into identities. Optimising the detector
on AP alone would have kept the worse setting, which is the first hard evidence
that mAP is not a sufficient selection signal for this project.

title: Dataset acquisition, conversion, and audit
description:
Official MOT20, CrowdHuman, and the Byte65 test-adapted supervision, converted

Evidence: `datasets/README.md`,
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-byte65nms-68seq-audit.md`.
close_reason:
All seven child issues closed. The dataset workstream delivered every build the
detector experiments needed, each with a recorded audit:

- Official MOT20 inventoried and the val_half temporal split built and verified

- CrowdHuman extracted and converted, 19,370 images / 439,046 person instances.
- Byte65 MOT20-test supervision human-audited, which is what pins every build to

- Base ablation build, 23,859 train / 4,463 held-out valid, shared byte-identical

Reopen or create a child if a new build is needed, for example for I7.

title: Measure localization before and after the tracker
description:
Separate how much IoU is lost from why, and determine whether any
post-detection stage degrades box quality.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/analyze_localization.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 5, `docs/experiment-report.md` section 3.
close_reason:
Done for nine variants including arm D, completed 2026-09-08. Hungarian match
against gt.txt at IoU 0.5, detections filtered at score >= 0.40, per-edge
residuals normalised by ground-truth box size.

Three findings. The error is jitter, not an offset: signed residual means are
near zero on every edge for every variant while absolute means are 1.22-1.44x
the baseline's, so there is no systematic shift to subtract out. The tracker is
not the culprit: mean matched IoU is 0.8356 for arm D's detections and 0.8362
for its tracks, 0.8713 and 0.8726 for the baseline. And resolution barely
touched it: arm D's absolute residuals are 0.0603/0.0611/0.0225/0.0445 against
arm A's 0.0602/0.0629/0.0234/0.0449, with mean matched IoU moving 0.8336 ->
0.8356.

title: Stage 1: val_half tracking runs against the yoloxx20 baseline
description:
The first end-to-end comparison, holding tracker and ReID fixed and varying
only the detector.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 7,
`docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Stage 1".
close_reason:
Done 2026-09-05. Best RF-DETR arm-A variant `rfdetr2xl-e5-t010-nms070` reached
HOTA 68.809 against the baseline's 70.208 with held-out OSNet ReID and
BoostTrack++ defaults.

RF-DETR led MOTA (86.883 against 85.031) and IDF1 (83.255 against 82.536) while
losing HOTA, DetA, AssA and LocA. That combination is what motivated the root
cause work: a detector cannot be simply "worse" and still win MOTA.

title: Prove the training labels and gt.txt are the same boxes
description:
The detector is scored against COCO annotations; HOTA is scored against
`gt.txt`. If those two label sets disagreed, every comparison between mAP and
HOTA would be measuring an annotation artifact rather than the detector.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 1.2,
`artifacts/tracking/annotation-agreement-val_half.json`.
close_reason:
Done, and the answer is unambiguous. Measured directly against each other with
no model involved: 615,137 matched pairs, GT coverage 1.0000, COCO coverage
1.0000, mean matched IoU 0.9995, median 1.0000, fraction at IoU >= 0.95 of
0.9998. Mean edge residuals are 0.0000 on x1/x2/y1 and -0.0005 on y2.

The two label sets are the same boxes. A label-convention mismatch is therefore
excluded as an explanation for any mAP-versus-HOTA disagreement, which is what
made the later root-cause work tractable.

title: Integrate and validate the revised Focus review workflow
description:
## Why
The event controls, timeline, trajectory, and loading behavior must work together across synthetic edge cases and real read-only MOT20 review before the epic can be accepted.

## What
Exercise each event family, every pair, and all three; cover thresholds, races, gaps, no-event states, past/full trajectory, timeline seeking, delayed loading, new-control axe scans, console/network state, desktop/narrow screenshots, source-integrity manifests, pointer-latency and browser-performance comparison, operator documentation, and final user visual acceptance. Keep real MOT20 track/frame results observational and deterministic gates synthetic.
design: Implement Task 5 of the attached plan only after Tasks 1-4. Use synthetic gapped/sparse/dense fixtures for correctness and MOT20-01 track 72 only as read-only usability evidence. Update README/HANDOFF and performance evidence when measurements change.
acceptance_criteria: Focused and aggregate viewer gates pass; real and synthetic browser journeys pass without console/network/layout failures; new controls have zero serious/critical axe violations; pointer latency remains within the accepted budget; configured source manifests are unchanged; screenshots document stable geometry; and user acceptance is recorded before closing the epic.
notes: Implementation and automated verification complete on 2026-09-03. make acceptance passed; make e2e-real passed 7 with 1 intentional narrow performance skip; source manifests are byte-identical across 2,249 configured files; all pointer p95 runs were 16.8 ms under the 50 ms budget; desktop and narrow screenshots are in track-viz/artifacts/verification/focus-review/. Task remains open solely for required user visual acceptance.

title: Eliminate Focus playback and loading layout shifts
description:
## Why
Transient playback and review-loading messages can enter normal flow, causing the timeline, filmstrip, and lower panels to jump vertically while the reviewer watches a track. Event-refresh mount invariance is handled earlier by mot-06v.1; this issue owns playback image, observation, per-frame Context, and cross-panel geometry.

## Steps to Reproduce
Enter Focus or Context review, start playback, and observe the lower review panels while image decoding, frame observations, or per-frame Context evidence are delayed or fail. Loading states appear and disappear, moving the lower UI.

## What
Add delayed-success and delayed-failure characterization for playback-owned states, move transient statuses into overlays or fixed reserved slots, retain accessible announcements, keep one integration assertion for the Task 1 event-refresh slot, and assert stable Focus, viewport, timeline, filmstrip, and lower-panel geometry at desktop and narrow widths.
design: Implement Task 4 of the attached plan after final history controls exist. Loading feedback must not intercept controls or add normal-flow height. Task 1 owns event-refresh mount/status behavior; this issue owns image decode, observations, Context playback, and cross-panel bounding boxes.
acceptance_criteria: During Focus/Context playback with injected delays or failures, timeline and filmstrip positions vary by at most one CSS pixel; lower controls do not jump; status remains accessible; and controls stay operable unless their own action is genuinely unavailable.
close_reason: Verified overlay-based loading/error states with no normal-flow shift: 67/67 frontend tests, TypeScript, 14/14 focused desktop+narrow geometry cases, and full deterministic E2E 40 passed with 10 expected local-data skips. Image, observation, Context, and event refresh success/failure states kept Focus, viewport, timeline, filmstrip, and source-status within 1 CSS px and controls remained operable.

title: Build temporal and spatial track-history visualization
description:
## Why
The current timeline shows only endpoint, gap-start, and enabled-event markers, so continuous tracks appear as two dots and the reviewer cannot see intermediate occupancy or current progress. The short existing trace also does not offer an explicit complete-track view.

## What
Build a sequence-wide interactive history rail with occupied runs, explicit gaps, current playhead, collision-safe activity markers, pointer/keyboard seeking, and a complementary gap-aware trajectory that defaults to past-through-current and can explicitly show the complete track with future evidence distinguished.
design: Implement Task 3 of the attached plan. Use failing pure plan tests first. Preserve exact one-based seeking; implement one range-style rail control with Arrow=1 frame, Shift+Arrow=10, and Home/End bounds; render at most 256 deterministically aggregated evidence glyphs; never connect trajectory segments across gaps; cap trajectory vertices at 512 while preserving required evidence; keep static evidence under reduced-motion preferences.
acceptance_criteria: Continuous and gapped tracks visibly expose intermediate evidence and current position; range-style timeline seeking is exact and accessible; activity glyph density stays within budget and overlapping evidence remains usable; past mode contains no future evidence; complete mode is distinct; trajectory gaps remain disconnected on desktop and narrow layouts.
close_reason: Verified sequence-wide accessible rail and gap-aware trajectory: 67/67 frontend tests and TypeScript passed; full deterministic Playwright passed 28 with 10 expected local-data skips. Covers exact pointer/keyboard seeking, singleton and continuous runs, current playhead, bounded accessible evidence summary and 256-glyph aggregation, past/complete modes, future styling, reduced-motion retention, gap breaks, and <=512-vertex fallback preserving first/last/current.

title: Make review-event navigation activity-aware
description:
## Why
The current Previous/Next enabled-event controls merge displacement, scale, proximity, and meaningful confidence into one unexplained frame list. Dense proximity or accidental zero displacement/scale thresholds can therefore look like ordinary one-frame stepping.

## What
Characterize all three raw detectors without changing the backend API, derive deterministic frontend activity episodes, remove the combined navigator, add persistent family-specific counts and Previous/Next controls with diagnostic reasons, keep low-confidence navigation per-frame and separate, expose raw/activity counts, and use family-aware density warnings. Sentinel-only sources expose no track-event controls.
design: Implement Task 2 of the attached plan. Production events.py is inspect-only unless characterization proves a separately approved backend defect. Episodes never merge across missing observations. Displacement/scale anchor at greatest severity with earliest-frame ties; proximity groups by typed usable competitor ID and anchors at closest approach. Raw events remain auditable.
acceptance_criteria: On a deterministic synthetic fixture, displacement at 0.02 seeks the fixture-derived activity anchor rather than the next ordinary frame, with raw-next and grouped-anchor behavior asserted separately; default scale reports no target with a reason; continuous per-competitor proximity is one understandable activity; low confidence stays per-frame and separate; every unavailable action remains visibly and accessibly disabled.
close_reason: Verified frontend-derived activity episodes with unchanged backend contract: 59/59 frontend tests, 5/5 backend event characterizations, TypeScript, and 6 desktop/narrow Playwright cases passed. Covers gap isolation, deterministic severity ties, per-competitor proximity, separate low-confidence navigation, family-specific counts/actions, all disabled reasons, density warnings, and raw-next versus grouped-anchor behavior.

title: Stabilize Focus event settings and refresh lifecycle
description:
## Why
Typing decimal thresholds currently causes per-keystroke Focus reloads; a requested 0.02 can become 0, controls disappear, and unrelated track evidence is fetched again.

## Steps to Reproduce
Open a tracked source in Focus, enable abrupt displacement, select the threshold, and type 0.02 character by character. The Focus panel reloads after the first character, the applied threshold becomes 0, and Next enabled event can seek the next ordinary frame.

## What
Characterize the failure with a deterministic synthetic fixture, separate event refreshes from track/filmstrip loading, keep Focus content mounted, add validated draft threshold state with 300 ms debounce plus immediate Enter/blur commit, cancel stale requests, and retain the last successful state on refresh failure. This issue owns event-refresh mount invariance and its fixed status slot; playback image, observation, and per-frame Context geometry belongs to mot-06v.4.
design: Implement Task 1 of the attached plan. Invalid drafts issue no request and revert on blur with an accessible reason. Failed refreshes retain prior valid data/settings and use a non-layout-shifting retry state.
acceptance_criteria: Character-by-character entry of 0.02 remains 0.02; the existing combined next-event action seeks the exact frame derived by the synthetic characterization fixture rather than the next ordinary frame; all checkbox combinations persist; only event data refreshes; timeline and filmstrip remain mounted during success and failure.
close_reason: Verified stable event-only refresh lifecycle: frontend suite 54/54 passed, TypeScript passed, and delayed-event tracer passed in desktop and narrow Chromium; 0.02 draft, stale-response protection, checkbox composition, mounted Focus evidence, failure retry, and no evidence/filmstrip refetch are covered.

title: Improve Focus track history and event review
description:
## Why
Focus review currently hides intermediate track history, can turn typed decimal event thresholds into zero, merges different event families into an opaque navigation stream, and allows transient loading states to move the lower review UI.

## What

Source files remain read-only; source-path display and the Explore-mode B shortcut do not change.
design: Follow the attached approved plan. Preserve exact one-based frame, source-row, source-hash, and sequence-local track identity. Raw events remain auditable while the frontend derives deterministic activity episodes.

Playback never advances before the current frame is rendered, uses bounded batched prefetch, and focused backend/frontend/browser checks pass.

title: Settle whether MOT20 density or CrowdHuman sparsity causes duplicate set predictions
description:
The phenomenon is established: arm A emits 33.219 overlapping pairs per frame at
IoU >= 0.75 in 4,463 of 4,463 frames, against a ground-truth person-on-person
overlap rate of 0.585 per frame (measured by `tracking/scripts/analyze_gt_overlap.py`,
`artifacts/tracking/gt-overlap-val_half.json`). So ~32.6 pairs per frame are not
explainable by real crowding, and NMS at IoU 0.70 removes them for +0.63 HOTA.

The *cause* is not established. `docs/experiment-report.md` section 2.3 offers
MOT20's density (137.8 instances/image, ~19x COCO) as the leading hypothesis,
but the competing hypothesis is that 81% of training images averaging 22.7
persons taught the Hungarian matching to expect sparsity. Both arms measured so
far are CrowdHuman-heavy, so they cannot separate the two.

Do: export arm C's detections. Arm C trained on MOT20 only with no CrowdHuman,
so its duplicate rate is the discriminating measurement. If arm C duplicates at
the same rate, density is implicated and CrowdHuman is exonerated; if it drops
sharply, the training mix is the cause and the fix is a data question rather
than an architectural one.

Also worth adding to `analyze_detections.py`: match predictions to GT and count
predictions-per-GT directly, rather than counting raw prediction pairs. The GT
control bounds the confound but does not remove it.

Blocked by nothing; arm C's checkpoint exists. Discovered by external review,
2026-09-08.
Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 2.3, `docs/results-reference.md`.

title: Carry arms B and C through to HOTA
description:
Both were dropped because neither beat arm A on mAP. That deferral now
contradicts this project's own finding that mAP is not a sufficient selection
signal: NMS at IoU 0.70 lowers mAP@50:95 (0.6337 -> 0.6297) while raising HOTA
(68.175 -> 68.809), and the detection and tracking matrices disagree outright
for arm D.

Both checkpoints exist. Export, NMS at 0.70, embeddings, tracking, TrackEval.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I5,
`docs/experiment-report.md` section 5.

title: Assemble the base test-adapted RF-DETR COCO build
description:
The build every ablation arm shares, so that arm-to-arm deltas are attributable
to the single variable under test.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 2.
close_reason:
Done: `datasets/finetuning/rfdetr-mot20-crowdhuman-byte65-test-adapted-2026-09-04`.

Train 23,859 images / 1,154,031 annotations: 19,370 CrowdHuman + 4,468 MOT20
train_half + 21 Byte65. MOT20 share 18.8%. Valid 4,463 images, the full
val_half, held out.

Audit clean: `cross_split_duplicate_images: []`, `mot20_temporal_overlap: []`,
`query_capacity.maximum_loss_participating_labels = 377` which is what set
`num_queries = 390`.

Arms A and D both trained on this build with byte-identical manifests
(`train_manifest_sha256 = 9986768f...38ace3`), which is what makes the arm

title: Decision: adopt greedy NMS at IoU 0.70 as the export default
description:
RF-DETR is a set-prediction model and exports without NMS by design. Decide
whether to override that for MOT20.
close_reason:
Decided on measurement. Suppression IoU none / 0.70 / 0.60 / 0.50 gives HOTA
68.175 / 68.809 / 68.510 / 66.076, so 0.70 is adopted, matching the `nmsthre`
the published YOLOX detections were produced with.

Accepted trade: this *lowers* mAP@50:95 by 0.0040 and raises HOTA by 0.634. The
decision is explicitly to optimise the tracking metric over the detection
metric where they conflict.

title: Build a tracking environment separate from the training venv

The environment that produced the detector must stay untouched. Upstream ships
a conda `boost-track-env.yml` and there is no conda on this machine.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Open Items".
close_reason:
Done. `.venv-tracking` is a separate Python 3.12 virtualenv carrying torchreid,
FastReID dependencies, lap, cython_bbox, pycocotools, and scipy, built without

title: Arm B: MOT20 oversampled 4x to 48% of training images
description:
I5 arm. Tests whether the CrowdHuman-heavy mix causes the early-peak decline.

Evidence: `finetuning/experiments.md`, `docs/results-reference.md` section 3.2.
close_reason:
Done, `rfdetr-2xl-i5-armb-2026-09-07-r1`, 34,541.3 s, 30 epochs.

Peak regular 0.6147 and peak EMA 0.6168, both at epoch 1 of 30. Final 0.5696.

Two findings. It did not beat arm A's 0.6202 despite 2.6x the MOT20 share. And
it peaked at epoch 1, which is even earlier than arm A, reproducing the decline
shape rather than fixing it. Never carried through to HOTA; see e5-armbc-hota
for why that deferral is now questionable.

title: Measure arm D with the published FastReID embeddings
description:
The one missing cell in the results grid. Arm D has only been measured with
held-out OSNet; the FastReID column has no arm D entry, so it cannot be
compared against the published-ReID baseline rows.

Remember `fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20` is not held out: it is MOT20-trained and has
seen val_half identities, so absolute values inflate on both sides.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 7.2.

title: Arm C: MOT20 only, no CrowdHuman
description:
I5 arm at the opposite extreme, removing the domain mismatch entirely.

Evidence: `finetuning/experiments.md`, `docs/results-reference.md` section 3.3.
close_reason:
Done, `rfdetr-2xl-i5-armc-2026-09-07-r1`, 16,480.1 s, 100 epochs.

Peak regular 0.6118 and peak EMA 0.6139, both at epoch 9 of 100. Final 0.5579.

Removing CrowdHuman entirely made the peak worse, not better, and reproduced
the same early-peak-then-monotone-decline shape. Together with arm B this
falsified the I5 mix hypothesis.

Its detections were never exported, which is a gap: arm C is the only arm that
could settle whether CrowdHuman's sparsity causes the duplicate-prediction
failure. Tracked as e5-armc-duplicates.

title: Precompute L2 embeddings per detector and ReID variant
description:
Embeddings for every exported detection, keyed by the pair, so tracker
configurations can be swept without recomputing appearance features.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/export_embeddings.py`.
close_reason:
Done for `osnet-ain-msdc` and `fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20` across the RF-DETR arm-A
and arm-D variants and the `yoloxx20` baseline. Computed for every exported
detection rather than only those above `det_thresh`, which is what allows
`det_thresh` itself to be swept as a tracker setting.

title: I7b: determine why the EMA branch won in arm D but lost in arm A
description:
`use_ema = true` throughout, yet arm A promoted the regular branch (0.6202
against EMA's 0.6198) while arm D promoted EMA (0.6282 against regular's
0.6243, `best_total_source = ema` at global_step 3730).

So EMA was updating; the question is why the branches swapped. Answerable from
`metrics.csv` files already on disk, no GPU required.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` sections 3.1 and 3.4.

title: Assemble the I5 mix-ablation builds for arms B and C
description:
Two single-variable builds that change only the CrowdHuman/MOT20 ratio, keeping
the valid split byte-identical to the base build.

Evidence: `finetuning/scripts/assemble_i5_mix_ablation.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 2.
close_reason:
Done. Arm B `rfdetr-i5-armb-2026-09-07`: 37,263 train images / 2,908,881
annotations, MOT20 oversampled 4x to 48.0%. Arm C `rfdetr-i5-armc-2026-09-07`:

Arm B repeats the same 4,468 MOT20 images four times by manifest duplication.
That required declaring `intentional_oversampling` metadata so the dataset
audit accepts duplicate `file_name` entries instead of rejecting them as an

Arm B adds no new imagery.

title: Produce tracks for MOT20-04, -06, -07 and -08
description:
Run the chosen checkpoint and ReID over the four test sequences and export MOT
format. No local ground truth, so this produces tracks rather than scores.

Evidence: `datasets/MOT20/test/`, `docs/MOTPolicy.md`.

title: Verify RF-DETR 2XL retrieval and bounded trainability
description:
Confirm the 2XL variant can be obtained and trained in this environment before
committing to it.

Evidence: `finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-03-rfdetr-2xl-preflight.md`.
close_reason:
Done. Base checkpoint `weights/rfdetr/rf-detr-xxlarge.pth`, sha256
`bf418652d5e07ad441599acfadc65bb1767029079e7a343a6d61675ec5d553ae`, retrieved
and confirmed trainable. Every arm in this repository starts from that exact
file, verified by the `checkpoint_sha256` field in each run's
`run-provenance.json`.

title: Make RF-DETR training and validation honour MOT20 ignore regions
description:
MOT20 marks crowd and distractor areas that must not be scored as false
positives. Stock RF-DETR has no notion of them.

Evidence: `finetuning/src/mot20/detection/rfdetr_integration.py`,
`finetuning/scripts/trace_ignore_aware_rfdetr.py`.
close_reason:
Done. `use_ignore_aware_rfdetr(ignored_iou_threshold)` wraps training and
validation so annotations with `iscrowd = 1` are treated as ignore regions at
IoU 0.5 rather than as negatives. val_half carries 61,382 such regions against
615,137 positives.

This is also what makes the detector's own reported mAP comparable with the
independent pycocotools protocol in e5-detection-matrix, which carries the same
regions as `iscrowd` and lets COCOeval handle them natively.

title: Extract and convert CrowdHuman to the training COCO layout
description:
CrowdHuman supplies the bulk of the person supervision. Convert it, preserving
the full-body box convention and ignore regions.

Evidence: `finetuning/scripts/extract_crowdhuman.py`, `datasets/crowdhuman/`.
close_reason:
Done. 19,370 CrowdHuman train+val images carrying 439,046 person instances are
converted and folded into the training builds via
`finetuning/scripts/extract_crowdhuman.py` and the shared conversion module
`finetuning/src/mot20/detection/coco_conversion.py`.

Measured domain statistics, recorded in `docs/results-reference.md` section 2.1:
22.7 persons per image mean against MOT20's 116.3, and a median long side of
1,024 px against MOT20's 1,654. The training transform therefore upscales
CrowdHuman by 1.302 and downscales MOT20 by 0.806. That 1.6x scale-regime split
and 5x density split became the I5 hypothesis, which later testing falsified.

title: Attack the localization gap through regression loss weighting
description:
LocA is 2.856 below the baseline and is the largest single remaining gap. Arm D
established that resolution is not the lever: 1.44x the pixels at the baseline's
effective scale moved LocA by 0.131 and mean matched IoU by 0.0020.

The error is symmetric jitter, not a correctable offset, so there is no
annotation convention to fix on the detector side. Reweighting `loss_bbox`
against `loss_giou` targets it directly.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` sections 3 and 6.

title: Vendor TrackEval and confirm it runs end to end
description:
Scores must come from the official evaluator rather than a reimplementation,
and both detectors must run through the identical evaluator.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md`, `tracking/scripts/evaluate_tracks.py`.
close_reason:
Done. Vendored TrackEval runs via `run_mot_challenge.py --BENCHMARK MOT20
--SPLIT_TO_EVAL val` against `repos/BoostTrack/results/gt/MOT20-val`, which is
byte-equivalent in span to `datasets/val_half/` (MOT20-01 is seqLength 214,
frames renumbered from 1). Ground truth 615,137 boxes, 1,418 identities.

Every row in `docs/results-reference.md` section 7, baseline included, was
produced by this evaluator through the same runner, with only the detection
file differing between a baseline row and an RF-DETR row.

title: Establish the eight-GPU DDP batch and runtime envelope
description:
Pick the physical batch, GPU count, and runtime budget from measurement rather
than guesswork, on 24 GB RTX 3090 cards.

Evidence:
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-rfdetr-2xl-ddp-capacity-probe.md`,
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-rfdetr-2xl-aspect-capacity-probe.md`.
close_reason:
Done. Settled on micro-batch 8 x 8 GPUs = global batch 64, BF16, gradient
checkpointing on, SyncBatchNorm, `find_unused_parameters=True`, at the audited
1360x1360 envelope. Stress probes at batch 4/5/6/7/8/9/10 are recorded under
`finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-byte65-test-adapted-ddp-batch*`.

This envelope is what later made arm D predictable: arm B measured 21 GB of
24 GB at the 1333 cap, so raising the cap to 1600 for ~1.44x the tokens could
not fit at micro-batch 8. Arm D was restructured to micro-batch 4 with
`grad_accum_steps = 2`, preserving global batch 64, and measured 14 GB per card
with no OOM.

title: Label all test outputs local_test_adapted
description:
The detector's training mix contains 21 Byte65 MOT20-test images and, if
FastReID is used, `mot20_sbs_S50.pth` is MOT20-trained. Results are therefore
not held out and not leaderboard-comparable, and `docs/MOTPolicy.md` prescribes
the required language.

Evidence: `docs/MOTPolicy.md`.

title: Inventory official MOT20 and build the val_half temporal split
description:
MOT20 ships no official validation split. Build a local one and record its
provenance so every later measurement is reproducible.

Evidence: `datasets/README.md`.
close_reason:
Done. `datasets/MOT20/` holds the official train (MOT20-01/02/03/05) and test
(MOT20-04/06/07/08) trees. `datasets/val_half/` is the second temporal half of
each training sequence, rebased to frame 1: MOT20-01 frames 216-429 -> 1-214,
-02 1393-2782 -> 1-1390, -03 1204-2405 -> 1-1202, -05 1659-3315 -> 1-1657.
Total 4,463 frames, 615,137 pedestrian boxes, 1,418 identities.

Verified byte-for-byte on 2026-09-08: the first and last image of every
val_half sequence is md5-identical to the corresponding original train frame.

`datasets/README.md` documents the ranges and also carries the warning that the
bundled `det_yoloxx20` detections come from a detector trained on the complete
MOT20 train set. That warning turned out to matter a great deal; see e5-leakage.

title: Expand the query table from the pretrained size to 390
description:
MOT20 frames carry up to 377 loss-participating labels. The pretrained
checkpoint's query table is far smaller, and `num_queries` must exceed the
observed maximum while staying divisible by `group_detr`.

Evidence: `finetuning/src/mot20/detection/checkpoint_loading.py`,
`finetuning/scripts/train_rfdetr_2xl.py`.
close_reason:
Done. `expand_query_parameters` grows the checkpoint's `query_feat.weight` and
associated tables to `num_queries = num_select = eval_max_dets = 390` with
`group_detr = 13`, validated against the dataset audit's
`maximum_loss_participating_labels = 377`.

The launcher materialises the expanded checkpoint once in the parent process
via `--prepare-run`, before any DDP rank starts, and every rank then loads that
one file. `validate_training_config` refuses a run whose `num_queries` does not
exceed the audited maximum, is not divisible by `group_detr`, or whose
`num_select` differs from `num_queries`.

title: MOT20 test-set delivery
description:
Produce tracks for the MOT20 test sequences. No local ground truth exists, so
this stage produces tracks, not scores.

Evidence: `docs/MOTPolicy.md` for the required language and benchmark
separation; `docs/tracker-experiments.md` for the artifact/variant naming and
the detection-handoff contract. Originally recorded in `docs/tracker-todo.md`
Phase 9, which was deleted when tracking moved to Beads.

title: Export L1 detections at a low threshold with structural validation
description:
Detections must be exported once at a permissive threshold so that thresholds
and suppression can be swept later as derived variants without re-running the
detector.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/export_detections.py`,
`docs/tracker-experiments.md`.
close_reason:
Done. `tracking/scripts/export_detections.py` captures from the library's own
validation loop, records geometry, threshold, `num_select`, NMS, class filter,
and a verification block containing the reproduced validation metrics.

Exported variants: `rfdetr2xl-e5-t005` (1,265,422 boxes), `-t010`,
`-t010-nms070`, `-t010-nms0600`, `-t010-nms0500`, plus arm D's
`rfdetr2xl-armd-e9-t005` (1,261,854) and `-t010-nms070`. `yoloxx20` is
registered from the shipped files at 580,369 boxes.

`derive_filtered_variant.py` produces the threshold and NMS variants from a
stored export rather than re-running inference, which is what made the
suppression sweep cheap.

title: Acquire and verify the external ReID weights
description:
The upstream checkout ships no weights. Two are needed: a generic
domain-generalized model for held-out validation runs, and BoostTrack++'s
published MOT20 model.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "External Assets".
close_reason:
Done, both acquired 2026-09-05 into `repos/BoostTrack/external/weights/`.

`osnet_ain_ms_d_c_wtsonly.pth`, 8,957,365 bytes, sha256
`482f09440f28ac92b7aa215a56323430f03aaf2657273269af02a670d3c8440a`. OSNet-AIN
x1.0 domain-generalized over MSMT17/DukeMTMC/CUHK03, 512-d output, finite, zero
unexpected keys. It is the weights-only variant, so `classifier.weight` and
`classifier.bias` are absent; OSNet returns features before the classifier in
eval mode, so the fix is a non-strict load asserting the missing set is exactly
those two, not fabricating zero tensors into the checkpoint.

`mot20_sbs_S50.pth`, 315,810,563 bytes, sha256
`d3a39a1ab54a63ac6724f2864a36485b0b5762fefced98941fca2a0784180656`, from the
BoT-SORT authors. FastReID SBS ResNeSt50, deep stem, Split-Attention, GeM,
BNNeck, `heads.weight` of (414, 2048). Those 414 identity classes are the MOT20
ReID identity count and are the primary evidence the file is MOT20-trained
rather than the MOT17 sibling, which is exactly why it is not held out.

A Hugging Face file of the same name at 336,553,343 bytes is not byte-identical
and was not used.

title: I2: sweep the association hyperparameters
description:
Establish how much headroom exists on the tracker side before spending GPU time
on the detector.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I2,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 7.2.
close_reason:
Done. 21 configurations swept over `iou_threshold`, `lambda_iou`,
`lambda_shape`, `lambda_mhd`, `max_age`, `min_hits`, `dlo_boost_coef`.

Best RF-DETR point gains +0.21 HOTA over defaults, but the baseline gains with
it, so the gap closed only from 2.13 to 1.02. The whole sweep spans 0.55 HOTA.

Two incidental findings: `dlo_boost_coef` at 0.3 and 0.7 produced byte-identical
results, so that knob does nothing on this data; and raising `min_hits` trades
IDSW for DetA at a net loss. Conclusion recorded at the time: everything
reachable from the tracker side has been measured, and the remainder is
detector box regression.

title: I3: measure with the published FastReID MOT20 embeddings
description:
BoostTrack++ publishes with `mot20_sbs_S50.pth`. Measure it, while recording
that it is not held out.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I3,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 7.2.
close_reason:
Done, worth +0.70 HOTA on the RF-DETR side (68.809 -> 69.509 at defaults).

Recorded caveat, which is why the OSNet rows remain the headline: this
checkpoint is MOT20-trained and has seen val_half identities, so absolute
values on both sides are inflated. Detector-to-detector deltas remain
meaningful because both sides use it. BoostTrack itself uses generic OSNet for
validation splits for exactly this reason.

Arm D has not yet been measured with FastReID; tracked as e5-armd-fastreid.

title: Decision: run I5 before I6
description: Two Tier 1 candidates, limited GPU time. Which first.
close_reason:
Decided 2026-09-06. I5 first: roughly 5x cheaper per epoch and the cleaner
hypothesis, so running it first establishes the recipe before spending on
resolution.

Outcome in hindsight: I5 was falsified and I6 succeeded, so the ordering cost
one wasted pair of arms. It was still the right call on the information
available, and I5's falsification is what raised the prior on I6 enough to
justify arm D.

title: Consolidate viewer under track-viz
description: Move the viewer backend, UI, tests, config, scripts, packaging, and docs into a self-contained track-viz directory while preserving root commands and runtime behavior.
close_reason: Consolidated backend, React UI, tests, config, scripts, docs, and preserved artifacts under track-viz; make acceptance passed (63 backend, 49 frontend, 4 CVAT, 22 deterministic E2E, 1 local smoke), and API/UI runtime checks returned 200.

title: Deliver context mode and review ergonomics
description:
## Why
Reviewers need restrained competition evidence and a fully keyboard/accessibility-capable workflow without restoring dense visual overload.

## What
Execute Task 6 only in the frontend: Focus/Context controls, capped corner markers with hysteresis, optional event controls, listbox/live-region/reduced-motion semantics, and responsive layout. No backend or dependency edits.
design: Follow Task 6. Shape and stroke weight, not color alone, distinguish focal and context tracks. Missing response fields return to the orchestrator.
acceptance_criteria: Draw-plan ink/label/focal-dominance bounds pass at the densest MOT20-01 frame; keyboard and responsive E2E pass; user-observed comparison validates or lowers the default context count.
close_reason: Accepted after post-integration verification: 44 frontend tests, strict TypeScript/build, 16 automated desktop/narrow E2E flows, and worker-run real dense MOT20-01 Focus/Context checks passed; accessibility, hysteresis, draw-plan dominance and responsive behavior covered. Human target-display review remains in final acceptance.

title: Add bounded Supervision exports and render parity
description:
## Why
Bounded clips and offline per-track videos may accelerate review if they preserve the browser identity contract and provenance.

## What
Execute Task 7: synchronous exports capped at 300 frames, offline per-track video, Origin protection, Supervision focal/context rendering, no-overwrite hash-keyed artifacts, provenance sidecars, and representative browser/export parity. No queues or source mutation.
design: Follow Task 7. All outputs are atomic derived artifacts; interactive requests beyond the cap are rejected with offline guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Browser/export colors and geometry agree within approved tolerance; stale/collision/partial-failure tests pass; one short clip and per-track video are structurally checked and observed; existing artifacts remain unchanged.
close_reason: Accepted after post-integration verification: 57 backend tests, Ruff/mypy/pip check/local smoke clean; bounded export safety/parity/provenance tests pass; real 10- and 26-frame MP4V exports decode at 1920x1080/25fps with metadata hashes; derived artifacts preserved.

title: Build context ranking and optional events
description:
## Why
Context and heuristic events require deterministic backend evidence without coupling algorithms to browser state.

title: Derive the results-reference generator's four literal blocks from artifacts
description:
`tracking/scripts/build_results_reference.py` reads every measured result from a
manifest, metrics CSV, or analysis JSON, but four descriptive blocks are still
hardcoded literals and can therefore drift silently from the data:

  - section 1.1 frame count (4,463) and identity count (1,418)
  - section 1.3 size bands, density, box-height percentiles
  - section 2.1 CrowdHuman-vs-MOT20 source-domain comparison
  - section 3 effective-input-geometry line

The generated file's header now discloses which blocks are transcribed, so the
document is honest, but the drift risk remains.

Do: compute each from a named artifact, the way `gt-overlap-val_half.json` is.
Then consider a non-writing `--check` mode that regenerates into memory and
diffs against the committed file, so CI or a pre-commit step can catch a stale
`docs/results-reference.md`.

Discovered by external review of the Beads migration, 2026-09-08.
Evidence: `tracking/scripts/build_results_reference.py`, `docs/results-reference.md`.

title: Decision: whether to build a clean YOLOX baseline ourselves
description:
With MOT17 out of scope there is no held-out external baseline available, so
the yoloxx20 leakage caveat is permanent. The only in-scope remedy is training
YOLOX-X on mot20_train_half ourselves, which would give a genuinely held-out
comparison at the cost of a full training run on an architecture this project
does not otherwise maintain.

Not costed, not scheduled. Recorded so the caveat's only exit is visible.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 0.

title: Make NMS a first-class export option rather than a derived post-filter
description:
Greedy NMS at IoU 0.70 is the measured best export setting and is worth +0.63
HOTA, but it is applied today by `derive_filtered_variant.py` after the fact.
Future exports should carry it by default so the good setting is the path of
least resistance.

Engineering, not an experiment.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I1.

description:

optimum may have moved. Cheap: derived variants from the stored export.

title: Train at max_size 1920 for native scale
description:
Native 1920x1080 at roughly 2.1x arm A's pixels, likely needing micro-batch 4
with gradient checkpointing already on.

Expect little: arm D already matched the baseline's effective scale exactly
(0.833 against 0.830) and moved LocA by 0.131. Recorded so the option is not
re-proposed as novel.

Do not attempt this at inference only. Probes at caps 1600 and 1920 leave
recall flat (0.9134 -> 0.9138 -> 0.9167) while mAP@75 falls 0.7400 -> 0.5943 ->
0.6890; the model regresses boxes well only at its trained geometry.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 4.3.
